title: Cold Acre — on the ridge two leagues north of Sill
caption: The farm hamlet two leagues north of Sill, one league beyond the Bone Orchard by the north gate road, drawn at walking scale: six houses and a byre in their drift-stone wall, the barley strips and turnip ground, the bare ring of ground about the well where frost will not hold and the children leave the untaken turn standing, and the well itself with its stone lip, clay dish, well-rope, eleven links to the water and the twelfth that hangs dry in the hand. The well-shrine and the children's stone stand beside the curb; a red nought marks the place where the thirteenth would stand. The road runs south to the north gate, Sill and the Bone Orchard drawn faint below, and east to the Tallow Works two leagues off; the frozen Ilm and the Singing Sill lie at the foot. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Frost, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the ninety-four days of ice, the bell that comes up the ridge four, four and a gap with the gap not ours to fill, the assessor's column that has never held a figure, the barrow of grey Ash that goes past on market-days, and no Last Day on a ridge. An engraved clay dish set on a stone sits in the margin.
